meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out before I did?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
"Pretty conclusive." That's a machine's guess, and the people who make these checkers say not to punish a student on the score alone. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you have besides a score.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and a finished draft pasted in from somewhere else looks exactly like that. Did anyone ask Owen before the zero went in?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
I don't see it in 3.2. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is a mistake, not an offence. How exactly does he cite it in the essay?
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
A student changing his argument in two weeks is what an outline is for. You didn't answer me. How does he cite that line?

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Five minutes after class, in your own notes, and "like, being stuck" is what paralysis means. I want the version history and the September 24 writing on paper, with their dates.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

He'll do the rewrite, Hale, to put this behind him and not because he did anything. Private, nothing on his record, and I'll want that in an email tonight. The copies I asked for and my other questions will be in mine.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday, November 12, after school, and that goes in tonight's email too.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes. A private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, its mark replaces the zero, nothing goes on his record, and I have it in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale (cc: Principal),

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero, nothing placed on Owen's record, and the mark entered well before December 1. I still require printed copies of the version history and the September 24 writing with their dates, and an answer to my question about how the line you say is not in Hamlet is cited in the essay. I expect your written confirmation of these terms tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record. She still wants your written confirmation tonight, the printed copies she asked for, and an answer about how the missing line is cited. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.

What moved her: You offered the private rewrite under 4.4 while saying plainly that you were not asking her to say Owen cheated. That let her protect his record without giving up her son.

What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it pretty conclusive. To her that is a machine's opinion she cannot check, so your first minute confirmed her fear that the school punishes first.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with the document created at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28 and the text arriving at 11:52 and 11:58 PM, landed on exactly that kind of late October night, which is why she wrote the times down and went straight to procedure. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she said a finished draft pasted in from somewhere else would look the same, do not concede it and move to the next document. Ask to see the weekend draft Owen says he wrote, so that your strongest piece stands.
